messages:
michael: FYI p90 latency jumped ~7% in prod after the new continuous-batcher rollout this morning. Noticing higher tail for short requests (<= 64 tokens).
alyssa: saw that alert, digging into KV hit-rate. Cache hit dropped from 73% -> 58% for those short sequences. looks like batch composition changed.
sanjay: any chance kernel selection changed too? small sequences sometimes trigger the fallback kernel which has worse latency.
alyssa: yes — profiler shows more small-prefixed batches ended up on the generic attention kernel. suspect batching mixing unrelated prefixes increased kernel heterogeneity per step.
michael: attaching small snippet from flamegraph sampling during the spike:
```
time  samples  op
00:01   42      attention_generic_kernel
00:01   18      attention_optimized_kernel
00:01   12      kv_cache_lookup
00:01    5      scheduling_overhead
```
elaine: that flame looks different from the canary. In canary optimized kernel dominated for short sequences. Now generic is winning.
sanjay: hypothesis: continuous-batch composition is prioritizing fill-rate and mixing prefixes, which increases per-batch variance in sequence length/prefix id -> poorer kernel routing and lower cache locality.
alyssa: exactly. Two effects: 1) prefix caching hit-rate drops because KV keys are spread across batches and warmup never accumulates 2) scheduler chooses a kernel safe for mixed shapes -> slower.
michael: do we have per-batch prefix-entropy metric? could retroactively compute for the timeframe.
elaine: I ran a quick agg: avg distinct-prefixes-per-batch from 1.9 -> 3.7 during the incident window.
sanjay: oh that explains it. More distinct prefixes = fewer repeated KV lookups in same batch -> lower per-batch hit-rate.
alyssa: proposed mitigations: a) soft affinity binning by prefix-hash when forming micro-batches (preserve some fill-rate) b) warmup prefetch: when we see a new prefix in flight, issue a low-priority prefetch to populate KV before it pairs with others c) tweak kernel selection policy to favor optimized kernel if majority of batch shares short sequence shape.
michael: can we test a) in staging quickly? affinity binning may increase queuing latency for some requests. need numbers on latency vs hit-rate tradeoff.
elaine: I set up a staging config that adds 50ms hold for affinity buckets; initial sim shows hit-rate up +12% and avg latency +9ms but p95 improves because fewer generic kernel invocations.
sanjay: that +12% hit-rate could mean far fewer backend tokens overall. worth it. Also try smaller hold windows (20ms) and dynamic: only activate when queue depth > X.
alyssa: also we should add a rollout gate: measure kernel-switch count per minute and KV hit-rate delta. Automatic rollback if kernel-switch > threshold or p95 regresses.
michael: action items: 1) sanjay -> instrument distinct-prefix entropy per-batch + kernel-switch metric (ETA 2d) 2) elaine -> run affinity-binning canary with 20ms/50ms knobs (ETA 1d) 3) alyssa -> implement prefetch prototype (ETA 3d) 4) me -> add rollback gate to deploy job config.
elaine: deploy-bot: canary scheduled for eng-runtime-staging at 1800004200 :eyes:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy for batch-affinity-flag scheduled on eng-runtime-staging at 1800004200 by elaine.
michael: cool. also add a synthetic test that exercises high prefix churn to verify no regressions in cost.
sanjay: note: need to watch kernel-selection heatmap on GPU-0; mixing could be imbalanced across devices if certain prefixes prefer certain kernels.
alyssa: will add heatmap to daily perf dashboard and an alert if kernel-skew > 0.4.
michael: thanks all — keep updates in this thread. if affinity helps we can tune down hold to minimize extra latency while recovering KV hit-rate.
